text.text: A ten-minute tour of the academy in this workspace. Share it with course owners, instructors and learner support.

Monday: the dashboard. Seats left on cohorts that are enrolling, refunds to decide, help requests due.
Every day: support clears help requests and refunds; instructors mark sessions held and post recordings.
Thursday: course owners review courses in production.
After each cohort: completion, refunds and what to change.
Every morning: help requests and refunds due today
Every week: quiet learners contacted, seats checked
Every cohort: launch countdown, finish review
Every quarter: which courses to build, refresh or retire

Course owners own content, price and launch dates. Instructors own live sessions and learner progress. Learner support owns help requests and refunds. The academy director reads completion and refunds across all cohorts.

Rename tracks, formats and refund reasons to fit your academy, set your own refund windows, and delete the sample rows once your first real cohort is in. Start small: enter your live courses and the next cohort of each, then add learners as they enroll. The counts, completion rates and seats left fill in by themselves as you go.
The academy at a glance. Charts read the live tables.

The spring Marketing Foundations run opened with 40 seats. Four weeks out it had 14 learners, so the course owner emailed alumni and two partner organizations. It started with 31. By week four, two learners had gone quiet for twelve days; a short call brought one back and the other moved to the summer run instead of asking for a refund.
Learners judge the academy by how fast and how kindly we answer them. This is how support works, from the first message to a refund.

Bastien was charged twice for Marketing Foundations. Support opened a refund request for $490 marked Duplicate charge, the payment provider returned it within an hour, and Bastien got a reply with the receipt the same morning. His help request and refund were both closed before lunch.
A new course takes three to four months from idea to first cohort. This workflow keeps the work visible so launch dates are honest.

Brand Design for Beginners started as an idea in spring. Seven of ten past learners said they would pay. The owner scripted twenty lessons, filmed them in four batches and tested the first two with three learners, who found the exercises too long. They were cut in half, and the pilot cohort opened with a 14-day refund window.
